first_body: The target was the primary rows 1.2× faster than the first recorded run (92ce041). Measured today on e4ee30c (before W1b’s revert; its first-pick and selection rows include W1b), 3 pairs (92ce041 had no computer player, so those two rows are missing): ×0.893 (last run measured ×0.968 on its own code; the two runs’ VMs differ, so compare within a run only). Called better: a shared game’s page −44%, reopening a long game −31%. Called worse: joining’s first board frame 1.57 → 5.12 s (+216%), the opponent’s move landing 136 → 215 ms (+58%; against main this run it was −5.8%, not called, so it came in before this branch; it was +4.6% uncalled last run), the phone start page +7.4%. Still worse in the diagnostics: the first pick 33 ms → 764 ms (2.34 s last run), JS heap on a reopened 2,000-ply game +34%, one texture more after 16 plies (the garden copy, not a leak: X5a). The lobby, the garden, the preview and the entrance all came after 92ce041; the join remains the largest wait.
lean_body: On the final commit (3 pairs), one diagnostic was called worse: create → share link shown +27% (1.39 1.16 1.28; +22% leaning in the 4-pair A/B on f6e8215). No code on that path changed on the branch (the lobby, the socket and the side choice are untouched; the warm-up runs on a board only), and the row has two modes (ledger B1/L1), so I read it as the VM; it is the first thing to recheck. Primary rows leaning slower without a call are listed under Needs from me. In the earlier A/Bs: reopen long tasks total +18% and the phone’s click → side choice +30% leaned slower on f6e8215 (+6.7% and not repeated on later runs).
